text: Did you know, cardiovascular disease is the number one cause of death globally.
Here in Australia, it claims 125 lives every single day.
That's one life every 12 minutes.
But what is cardiovascular disease?
Cardiovascular disease describes a range of conditions that affect your heart or blood vessels.
There are many different types and it can affect anyone at any age.
You can be born with a heart defect known as congenital heart disease,
or you can develop a problem with how your heart beats.
This is known as an arrhythmia.
Also of major concern, cardiovascular disease could cause a heart attack or stroke.
A heart attack usually occurs when there is a blockage in a blood vessel to the heart muscle.
Symptoms vary depending on the type of heart condition and whether you're male or female.
Some symptoms may include chest pain,
shortness of breath, dizziness, fatigue or nausea.
But it's important to remember that in the early stages you may have no symptoms at all.
Leading risk factors for heart disease and stroke include high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes,
smoking and unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, being overweight and genetics.
Which means your risk of cardiovascular disease can also be inherited from your parents.
So, can you reduce your risk of developing cardiovascular disease?
Yes, just by leading a healthy lifestyle or quitting smoking you can help take care of your heart.
Eating a balanced diet with plenty of fresh fruit and vegetables plus exercising regularly
are small steps you can take today.
Cardiovascular disease is easier to treat when detected early,
so seek immediate medical care if you have any concerns.
Do not delay.
Remember every 12 minutes cardiovascular disease claims a life.
It's not just a number, it's a life.
It could be a family member, a friend, it could be you.
Take care of your heart and join the fight against the world's number one killer.
There isn't a cure for cardiovascular disease.
But thanks to breakthroughs at the Victor Chang Cardiac Research Institute,
we are discovering more about how to treat and prevent it.
